title: Sparse matvec layout + prefetch
description:
Cache-bound sparse kernels targeting the LDPC parity-check matvec path where memory access patterns dominate. Two complementary approaches: software prefetch + block-CSR layout for runtime gains, and one-shot Cuthill-McKee row reorder for amortised cache-reuse gains.

## Background

`SparseBitMatrix::matvec` is scalar CSR iteration with no prefetch and no block layout. The gather pattern is index-driven, which is cache-unfriendly for LDPC parity-check matrices that have irregular row spans. Two distinct layout-level wins are available: (1) D1 — software prefetch on `col_idx[i + lookahead]` plus block-CSR ($4\times 64$ dense bit-blocks within sparse rows) plus SIMD inside dense blocks; (2) D2 — Cuthill-McKee (RCM) row/column permutation applied once before dispatch, amortising across many matvecs.

D1 measures speedup per single matvec call; D2 measures amortised speedup over $\geq 100$ matvec calls (single-call cost is dominated by the reorder itself).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Each child task ships per the per-kernel execution protocol from the epic spec doc.
- [hard] Bit-exact result vs. existing CSR matvec (D1 raw, D2 after permutation roundtrip).
- [hard] D1 asm artefact shows prefetch instructions actually emitted; perf-stat evidence is recorded for CSR, block-CSR without prefetch, and block-CSR with explicit prefetch.
- [hard] D2 permutation roundtrip (apply then unapply) is identity.

## User-approved amendment

D1 and D2 both shipped correctness-tested opt-in sparse-layout scaffolds, but measured evidence showed the existing CSR path remains faster on the deterministic LDPC-like fixtures. Per user-approved child amendments, accept the opt-in block-CSR/prefetch and RCM scaffolds plus committed evidence, keep CSR as the default production sparse matvec path, and treat sparse layout/prefetch speedup as future work rather than a closure blocker for this story.

## Notes

Bench target: existing `sparse.rs` bench at LDPC parity-check matrix sizes. Cache-bound kernels may rely on cache-miss-rate improvement instead of pure IPC delta. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
